24/12 Boksburg Blast

By: Hein Kaiser | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
we investigate the tragic circumstances of 24/12; the LPG gas blast in Boksburg on Christmas eve

Unique Selling Point:
While the story was all over the news, timelines and how it actually may have happened, and possibly why, was never unpacked fully in the media. Carte Blanche will investigate and unpack the timeline of the tragedy in a "60 minutes from disaster" fashion - as the narrative of the day plays out in this manner completely.

Summary:
On Saturday 24 December an LPG Gas tanker exploded after the tank was capped, when it became stuck under a bridge. The consequent gas leak ignited shortly after, and an hour after it became stuck, the tanker exploded, killing 30 people, leaving several still missing and countless injured. But could the entire tragedy of circumstance been avoided? Nobody followed an emergency plan, it seems, with systemic failures all over. The police station is 1 minute's drive away, yet they only arrived after the second blast, same with metro police. There was no perimeter set up when the truck started leaking, either, and no signage per the law that the driver might have seen, to warn him of the bridge height.

In fact, the area should have been evacuated minutes after the truck got stuck. But none of this happened.

Further information:
1. While the driver was at fault there was no signage at all bar one illegible sign. Yet 3km down the road a similar bridge is perfect toy sign posted.
2. The narrative focus on the driver looks to deflect the following: a) that there was an hour between getting stuck and the blast in which the EMPD should have evacuated the area. b) but they didn’t pitch up until after I was there on the day. It would have been their job under the fire department to evacuate the area.
3. The SAPS is one minute away. They didn’t pitch until I got there either.
4. The municipality blames Prasa. Yet they are responsible for the signage on the street, not Prasa it seems.
5. EMPD is 2km away from ground zero. Yet they only arrived after the second blast.
6. It’s an investigation into a possible cover up on all sides, particularly by government, as a deep failure of emergency services.
7. According to an expert accident investigator hardly anyone should have died or be injured if they did what they were supposed to do.
8. The road was resurfaced and that changed the height of the bridge too it seems. No signage.

I have the following people:
⁃ members of the community who we’re there. And I have a guy who was there from the get go to draw the timeline.
⁃ Then compare the various narratives out there.
⁃ Then investigate and interview expert, mayor, fire chief, metro, saps, victims and DOT and investigate ourselves.
⁃ We show other bridges in the area that are correctly signposted.

There was a golden hour to save lives. But nobody did it.

My approach will be Voxies included to narrate the piece better.

I have footage I filmed myself on my phone, on the day. And the community is giving me their footage, too. I have been there about 5 times already walking the streets.

So this won’t be what the news showed, and it won’t be a victim sideshow. But an “investigation” in true CB style.

Script:


CLAIRE Link [00:09:55] They say you have a golden hour to save lives. But on Christmas Eve in Boksburg, they had much more than that.
VO: It is 6 in the morning. In the suburb of Plantation to the east of Johannesburg, some residents are still asleep. At Tambo Memorial Hospital medical staff change shifts.
Thirteen kilometers away, a 32-year old truck driver has set off from his overnight stop en route to Botswana, with a tanker of highly-pressurized liquid petroleum gas. He overnighted here - SA Bulk ﻿- one of the few places where a truck carrying such hazardous materials can stop over safely.
But who would guess that this morning, countless lives would be taken… or changed…forever?
Marius: Whatever background you have, nothing prepares you for something like that.
VO: It all starts when the truck driver gets lost…he takes a wrong turn…then tries to course-correct.
But now there’s an obstacle in his way: A low bridge under a railway line across the road from Tambo Memorial Hospital: the heart of suburbia.
As he passes under the bridge, it gets stuck at the tail end, scraping off the tanker cap.
It slowly starts leaking out gas...silent and poisonous.
Within two hours, the gas catches fire and explodes.
Anonymous [00:02:06] It was a really big explosion where everybody started running. People really got burned and the whole bridge fell down.
Clayton [00:02:12] Babies, parents, kids. You could smell the burning flesh.
VO The 24th of December 2022 will be remembered as one of South Africa’ darkest days. Moments after this explosion 9 people lay dead. Within two weeks, as man﻿y victims succumbed to third degree burns, the death toll rose to 40
Stanley [00:02:32] Liquid petroleum gas is actually a chemical you can't see. It's a chemical that's heavier than air. So it runs on the ground like water. And when it ignites, all of that stuff burns around you. And you won't even be aware that you're standing in.
VO From the moment the truck got stuck…death stalked the neighbourhood.
Clayton [00:02:55] It were bodies and people barely alive burns naked. I can't believe that when I get I've never seen a gas explosion before, but it was just complete chaos.
CLAIRE Link [00:03:11] If this is the destruction that is left, I actually can't imagine what it must have been like on that morning.
VO So how could this happen? We piece together some of the evidence - and the full picture is shocking.
ARNOUX [00:03:39] In the morning, he started his start, a procedure which we can actually see on the tracking systems and so forth. So he did his checks on his truck like you're supposed to do. He then got onto a road that would lead him to either the all one or two in 12, which is an approved route used by the company, which has been checked because under the safety protocols, the route needs to be audited before it is approved.
VO We reconstruct his journey and the suggestion that he was lost seems to check out. But while trying to get back to an approved route, he may not have known there was low-hanging bridge coming up …because all we could find were two rusted old signs on the northern and southern side, attached to the bridge itself, but not - as the law requires early warning signs around earlier bends in the road, to allow him to divert.
The driver approached the bridge from the south.
VO Ekurhuleni Mayor Tanya Campbell says signage was the first thing the city checked in its own investigation.
MAYOR [00:05:13] Obviously, with a blast, all the signage is all gone. The current reports are indicating that Ekurhuleni signage was in place.
VO But the faded and rusty sign on the bridge itself was all we could find﻿, even when we checked an alternative route to the bridge. Not a warning in sight.
ARNOUX XXXXX
Yet if the driver stopped and inspected the bridge before driving under it, as his employer claimed, he must have noticed the height restriction. But did he know that the height of the tanker was four metres at its highest point - almost half a meter higher than the sign’s limit?
Meanwhile, back in Boksburg, Stanley Mahlangu was asleep. (BLUE SIGN)
Stanley [00:05:40] The first time when the head did. Someone just woke me up. Oh, no. You do know that there's a truck which is stuck down the trail of the train? Say I walked heading that direction. Then when I saw that, it was exhausting. I even tried to tell some of the onlookers go away.
VO By 6-15 the tanker was stuck…leaking its contents. At that point, the driver's training did kick in..which required him to call the control room at ISS, his employer and the company contracted the truck’s owners, The Infinite Group, to transport the gas.
From this moment, his job was to secure the area and keep people away…until emergency services arrived.
Getting help was top priority. ISS records show that the first call to one of several Ekurhuleni emergency numbers was made at 6:29.
It is disturbing and shocking at the same time... Several more calls to Emergency Services went unanswered …at 6.32 another call, at 6.33 two successive calls….
And after establishing from their driver that no emergency services were on the scene yet, they tried again. And again.
With every passing minute, more curious onlookers and potential victims assembled for selfies and videos.
Stanley [00:06:55] Most people, when something in an incident happens, they want to take photos to send to their relatives, say, Oh, this is what they witnessed was the Christmas Eve.
VO A local security company officer helped the driver with crowd-control, cordoning off the area. Over the next 20 minutes, 8 more desperate calls were made to Emergency Services. Only at the last attempt did ISS get through to 10111 who then transferred the call to the fire department - just down the road from the scene of the unfolding crisis
VO Moments later, the truck caught fire…around the time the first fire engines arrived. While firefighters attended the flames, more people flocked closer.
Stanley [00:08:01] The driver was in big panic. Also, they tried to actually to tell people go away. But, you know, with people, if there's no in law enforcement, you know how they be.
VO Around 7:05 ISS tried to reach their driver again for an update. He’d passed out from inhaling too much gas. A Good Samaritan answered his phone…she would stay with him all the way to the hospital. (PLAY MORE OF THE CALL)
Clayton Viljoen is a community member and runs the community non-profit Urban Ruins in the area. He was one of the first people on the scene.
Clayton [00:08:41] When I arrived on scene, there were two ambulances and for the majority of the time that I was here, there were only the two. And you saw the one fire engine coming in. That's why I moved the body for. And then when I was driving out, I saw other ambulances approaching. But I never saw cops. I never saw police. I never saw any of that at all.
VO In the absence of law enforcement, private security managed the scene. Leroy Cave was on patrol when the truck exploded and his dashcam caught every moment. His area manager is Marius van der Merwe.
Marius [00:09:20] And then when the explosion fall out, that's when you do this backwards, obviously, to ensure that the vehicle doesn't get damaged to look after his own life as well, because obviously it was in danger.
VO We timed the journey between ground zero, the Ekurhuleni Metro Police and Bokburg police station. Both are closer than a 2-minute drive or a four-minute run.
On the day, a patrolman even drove to the police station and was told - ironically - they could only respond if someone phoned them.
On that quiet morning, the blast was heard kilometers away.
Stan [00:10:19] So prevention analysis always works best when you start at the end result and you work your way backwards. That’s how any forensic investigation does
VO Stan started investigating in the same place.
Stan [00:10:30] What would have avoided deaths would have been if they were far enough not to be killed. It's as simple as that. The next step is why were they so close and where were they supposed to be? And how would they know? Well, normally they would know because somebody from an official service would tell them.
VO: Witnesses placed the arrival of police and metro police up to 50 minutes after the blast - an unforgivable lapse for those who bore the fallout.
In a text message the police declined an interview and promised a future statement once they’ve investigated.
In Ekhurhuleni, the fire chief didn't even pitch up for a confirmed on-camera interview.
The Ekhuruleni Metro Police DID send a spokesperson to talk to us, but wasn't willing to provide our team an answer to the most significant question: why law enforcement was reportedly last on the scene?.
(USE LESS OF THE CHAT WITH THE EMPD - EVEN PART VO OVER PIC)
Link [00:11:36] What's shocking to me is that here at Ground Zero, you would think that emergency responses are far away when actually the police station is less than a kilometer away. Less than 2 minutes to get there.
Mayor [00:11:54] The report that was tabled to me has indicated that the SAPS 111 number was not answered. However, the correlation number was answered and it is never acceptable if calls are not answered. I have said to our department, absolutely there will be consequence management.
Stan [00:12:16] The only reason why I cannot call this a comedy of errors is simply because there is absolutely nothing funny about it. It's a disaster of absolute proportions, and the finger pointing can only be satisfied once the full investigation is done and even sometimes after it's been in and out of court.
A few nights after the tragedy, the community got together and held vigil for the victims.
Clayton [00:12:33] The only positive I can draw from this is the community united. Instantly, there were people offering food and blankets and assistance and it didn't matter. Color, wealth, reputation. It was a case of how can we help where you need us?

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): we investigate the tragic circumstances of 24/12; the LPG gas blast in Boksburg on Christmas eve
metadata.Unique Selling Point: While the story was all over the news, timelines and how it actually may have happened, and possibly why, was never unpacked fully in the media. Carte Blanche will investigate and unpack the timeline of the tragedy in a "60 minutes from disaster" fashion - as the narrative of the day plays out in this manner completely.
metadata.Summary: On Saturday 24 December an LPG Gas tanker exploded after the tank was capped, when it became stuck under a bridge. The consequent gas leak ignited shortly after, and an hour after it became stuck, the tanker exploded, killing 30 people, leaving several still missing and countless injured. But could the entire tragedy of circumstance been avoided? Nobody followed an emergency plan, it seems, with systemic failures all over. The police station is 1 minute's drive away, yet they only arrived after the second blast, same with metro police. There was no perimeter set up when the truck started leaking, either, and no signage per the law that the driver might have seen, to warn him of the bridge height. In fact, the area should have been evacuated minutes after the truck got stuck. But none of this happened.
metadata.Further information: 1. While the driver was at fault there was no signage at all bar one illegible sign. Yet 3km down the road a similar bridge is perfect toy sign posted. 2. The narrative focus on the driver looks to deflect the following: a) that there was an hour between getting stuck and the blast in which the EMPD should have evacuated the area. b) but they didn’t pitch up until after I was there on the day. It would have been their job under the fire department to evacuate the area. 3. The SAPS is one minute away. They didn’t pitch until I got there either. 4. The municipality blames Prasa. Yet they are responsible for the signage on the street, not Prasa it seems. 5. EMPD is 2km away from ground zero. Yet they only arrived after the second blast. 6. It’s an investigation into a possible cover up on all sides, particularly by government, as a deep failure of emergency services. 7. According to an expert accident investigator hardly anyone should have died or be injured if they did what they were supposed to do. 8. The road was resurfaced and that changed the height of the bridge too it seems. No signage. I have the following people: ⁃ members of the community who we’re there. And I have a guy who was there from the get go to draw the timeline. ⁃ Then compare the various narratives out there. ⁃ Then investigate and interview expert, mayor, fire chief, metro, saps, victims and DOT and investigate ourselves. ⁃ We show other bridges in the area that are correctly signposted. There was a golden hour to save lives. But nobody did it. My approach will be Voxies included to narrate the piece better. I have footage I filmed myself on my phone, on the day. And the community is giving me their footage, too. I have been there about 5 times already walking the streets. So this won’t be what the news showed, and it won’t be a victim sideshow. But an “investigation” in true CB style.
